sections.h2: Who sends the Jackson County tax bill
sections.html:
The Tax Collector produces the bill in Jackson County, and an online portal pulls up any parcel's bill by tax year. Values come from the Property Appraiser. The County Commission, the School Board and other districts set the rates.

The collector's calendar runs month by month through the year. Vehicle and license deadlines share it with property tax, so the table below picks out only the property rows. Compare them with your contract date to see which deadline comes next.

Jackson County keeps Central Time, so check the clock before paying online on the last day of a month.

sections.h2: What are the Jackson County property tax months?
sections.html:
Collection opens in November and ends at the gross amount on March 31, with the discount shrinking in between.

Property tax months for Jackson County
MonthWhat to expect
NovemberCollection opens; 4% discount if paid by November 30
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31
AprilUnpaid real property tax delinquent on April 1; 3% penalty

Business equipment, which is tangible personal property, follows the same discount months. A homeowner can usually ignore that row, but a landlord or a seller who ran a business from the property should read it.

Real property tax left unpaid on April 1 picks up a 3% penalty. The delinquent list goes into a local newspaper within 45 days, at the owner's expense, and repeats weekly for three weeks in May before the certificate sale. The sale date is chosen in March, so a seller can learn it before delinquency even begins.

An investor who buys a certificate holds a lien and does not own the house. If two years go by without redemption, the investor may apply for a deed and the clerk holds an auction. On a homestead parcel, statute 197.502 puts half of the latest assessed value into the opening bid, on top of what is owed.

Equipment taxes run on a different clock: 1.5% interest a month, advertising within 45 days, and tax warrant work from May 1.

sections.h2: Can Jackson County owners spread payments over the year?
sections.html:
Yes. The collector offers a plan of four payments toward the next year's tax, with applications due April 30. Enrolled owners stay in without reapplying.

  • First payment: due on or before June 1, with cancellation if nothing arrives by June 30.
  • Second payment: before September 30.
  • Third payment: by December 31.
  • Final payment: by March 31.

Two different dates apply to the first payment, so call the office to confirm which one governs your account. If you sell while on the plan, hand the closing agent a list of paid installments so the proration comes out right.

Homestead works here as it does across Florida. You live in the house on January 1, file DR-501 by March 1, and up to $50,000 comes off assessed value. Only the first $25,000 lowers school tax.

Growth in a homestead's assessed value is held to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and the state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. Parcels without homestead face a 10 percent cap. A sale ends both, so a buyer's first bill often exceeds the seller's last.

  • Seniors: a county or city ordinance may add an exemption for owners 65 or older within an income limit.
  • Veteran disability: a service-connected disability of 10 percent or more can bring a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • Leasing the house or leaving it removes homestead status.

Ask the Property Appraiser whether a local ordinance applies to your address.

TRIM notices go out in August, and a Value Adjustment Board petition must follow within 25 days. For a denied exemption you have 30 days from the date on the denial letter.

Talk to the appraiser's staff first. An error in square footage or exemption status can sometimes be fixed without a hearing, and a deed, survey or builder's records help if the property record itself is wrong.

sections.h2: Do mobile homes and business equipment follow the same dates?
sections.html:
Partly. Tangible personal property, such as business furniture and equipment, shares the real estate discount schedule, but it draws the harsher 1.5% monthly interest charge once delinquent.

Mobile homes have their own line. A mobile home not assessed as real property needs its decal renewed by December 31, and registration of mobile homes, trucks over 8,000 pounds and truck-trailers falls in the same December window. If you own a mobile home on land you are selling, ask the tax collector whether it is billed as real property or carries a decal, since that decides which deadline you face.

Raise both points with the closing agent early. Say whether the property includes a mobile home or business equipment, so every account tied to it is found and paid before settlement.

sections.h2: What a seller should line up before closing
sections.html:
Get the payoff in writing, with the tax year it covers. The title agent then divides the current year between buyer and seller at the closing table.

  • Use the portal's tax-year search to check whether earlier years remain open.
  • If April 1 has already come and gone, ask about the penalty and advertising costs.
  • Look for recorded liens in the Clerk's records.
  • Hand the closing agent your installment history.

Keep the parcel number, a copy of your deed and your latest bill in one folder, since each office will ask for them. Ask for balances to be quoted with a date, because totals change over the year. A seller racing a delinquency or certificate sale date can set a quick cash closing, with the title agent paying the tax out of proceeds. A cash buyer has no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait on, so the timeline depends mostly on title work.

faqs.q: What is the final day to pay Jackson County property tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: March 31 is the cutoff for the gross amount. Paying early earns 4% in November, then 3%, 2% and 1% in the following three months.

faqs.q: What penalty hits an unpaid Jackson County bill on April 1?
faqs.a: Real property takes a 3% penalty. Business equipment is charged 1.5% interest a month instead.

faqs.q: When does Jackson County hold its tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The collector fixes the date in March, ahead of the April 1 delinquency date. Ask the collector's office for the exact day.

faqs.q: Does Jackson County allow installment payments?
faqs.a: Yes. File by April 30 for next year's plan and pay in June, September, December and March. Ask the office for the exact June date.

faqs.q: Will selling raise the next owner's Jackson County bill?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent limit both end at a sale, and the next January 1 resets the property to just value.
